pattern.crimePattern: a spa manager paid through a foundation "sponsorship" locks an old member with a heart condition in a steam room at full heat, then plants an old pill bottle to make it look like his heart
pattern.notes: Fictional members' club, spa and staff; Muthaiga is a setting only. Stanley Rotich, one of the three fourth-floor names, is the victim and so is eliminated as Kivuli. Margaret Kabiru is a red herring here, in full view at breakfast. The note signed "M." and the Ukarimu envelope are t_kivuli spine facts.

ob.text: The Aberdare Members' Club, Muthaiga, reports a member found dead in its steam room after his early swim: Stanley Rotich (66), one of the three fourth-floor names. Suspected heart failure.

facts.text: Stanley Rotich was found dead in the steam room of the Aberdare Members' Club on Saturday morning after his swim.
Rotich collapsed on the bench, skin flushed; the steam room was at normal temperature when he was found.
His heart-pill bottle lies open on the bench, a few pills spilled. The pharmacy label is eight months old.
His locker holds a daily pill organiser with Saturday's slot already empty. His wife: he takes them at home; the bottle's prescription stopped six months ago.
Check sheet: 06:15, 06:30 and 06:45 initialled "I.K."
The staff signature book holds every spa staff member's specimen initials.
In the spa office bin: a damp rubber door wedge, its marks matching the steam-room door's bottom edge.
Scuffs on the tile under the steam-room door where something was jammed.
Gate log: Rotich in at 05:40; Ezra in at 05:45 and out at 06:02. No other member used the spa before 07:00.
Gladys was in her office at the gate from 06:00, on the gate camera.
Two swimmers: Rotich and a younger man argued on the pool deck at 05:50 about "the firm". Rotich left the pool at 06:08.
Terrace staff and four members: Margaret Kabiru hosted a donors' breakfast on the terrace, 06:00–07:30, in full view.
Laundry staff: Ibrahim came at 06:10, "sent by Madam Sagal to count towels", and left at 06:50.
Ezra's receipt and the forecourt camera: he was at a Westlands petrol station from 06:20 to 07:00.
Oduya's guard: at home until 06:40; then at DCI headquarters for interview from 07:00.
Flight record: Lawrence Ole Sein has been in Johannesburg since Tuesday.
Records ①: the steam room was set to MAX at 06:12 and back to NORMAL at 06:40, both with user code SPA-MGR: Sagal's.
Records ②: on Wednesday the club spa received a KSh 1.5 million "wellness sponsorship" from the Ukarimu Foundation.
Records ②: on Thursday KSh 500,000 in cash was deposited into Sagal's account at a bank agent.
In Sagal's wardrobe: an empty cash envelope printed with the Ukarimu Foundation logo.
With it, a note: "For the arrangement. — M."
Fingerprints taken from Sagal in detention.
Post-mortem: heatstroke with heart strain; a core temperature far above anything a normal steam session produces.
Post-mortem: death on Saturday between 06:25 and 06:45.
Lab: no fingerprints at all on the pill bottle, not even Rotich's.
Handwriting: the "I.K." initials at 06:15, 06:30 and 06:45 are Sagal's, not Ibrahim's.
Lab: Sagal's prints on the wedge.
Missing: there are no fingerprints at all on his pill bottle.
Missing: the attendant's checks between 06:15 and 06:45 weren't done.
Missing: Saturday's pills were already gone from his organiser.
Missing: the steam room wasn't hot when he was found.
Missing: nobody else used the spa that morning.
Sagal: "The steam room was at normal temperature all morning. Mr. Rotich must have had a heart attack."
Sagal: "I sent Ibrahim for towels, set it to the top and wedged the door. At twenty to seven I turned it down, took the wedge, and put an old bottle by him."
Sagal: "I've never been paid by anyone but the club."
Sagal: "A young man from the foundation came on Tuesday. He said an old member would 'cause trouble for good people', and 'it should be the steam, he has a heart'. Half a million."
Sagal: "I've never touched that wedge."
Ibrahim: "I checked the steam room every fifteen minutes."
Ibrahim: "Madam sent me to count towels at six. I came back at ten to seven. When I saw my initials in her writing I was afraid to say."
Ezra: "I didn't go to the club on Saturday."
Ezra: "We argued about the firm and his split with Lawrence. He said, 'After today, nothing will be the same, for any of us.' I left at two minutes past six."
Kabiru: "Stanley and I served together twenty years. I was at breakfast with my donors when Gladys came running. He'd been troubled lately. We all are, at our age."
Oduya: "I was at the DCI, as you know."
Lawrence: "I was in Johannesburg."

interrogations.intro: Sagal brings her own clipboard. "The steam room was at normal temperature all morning. Mr. Rotich must have had a heart attack."
Ibrahim stands to attention in his whites. "I checked the steam room every fifteen minutes."
Ezra keeps his car keys in his fist. "I didn't go to the club on Saturday."
Margaret Kabiru receives Amani on the terrace as if she were a guest.
Raphael Oduya, with his advocate beside him, says one sentence. "I was at the DCI, as you know."
Lawrence, by phone from Johannesburg: "I was in Johannesburg."
Gladys has the gate log open before Amani sits down.

contradictions.reaction: "Madam sent me to count towels at six. I came back at ten to seven. When I saw my initials on the sheet in her writing I was afraid to say."
"We argued about the firm. He said, 'After today, nothing will be the same, for any of us.' I left at two minutes past six. Those were his last words to me."
Sagal puts down her clipboard. "I sent Ibrahim for towels," she says, very evenly, "and I set it to the top."
"A young man from the foundation came on Tuesday. He said an old member was going to cause trouble for good people. Half a million. I have a sick mother in Garissa. I'm not asking you to forgive me."
Sagal folds her hands in her lap and says nothing more.

reconstruction.text: After case 96 Stanley Rotich understands the net is closing on the fourth floor. On Wednesday he posts a registered letter to Halima offering to testify. The same day the Ukarimu Foundation "sponsors" the club spa; on Thursday Sagal banks half a million in cash.

On Saturday Rotich swims at six as always, argues with his son on the deck, and goes into the steam at 06:10. At 06:08 Sagal has sent Ibrahim to count towels; at 06:12 she sets the steam room to MAX with her own code, and wedges the door from outside.
Rotich, 66, with a heart condition, collapses within twenty minutes. At 06:40 she turns the heat down, takes the wedge, and sets an old pill bottle open beside him, spilling a few pills.
She initials the check sheet for 06:15, 06:30 and 06:45 in Ibrahim's name, throws the wedge in her bin, and at 06:55 "finds" him.

afterVerdict.beat: On Monday Rotich's registered letter reaches Halima: "I am not the one they call K. Neither is Raphael Oduya: he carries envelopes and always has. The desk was Records. I will say whose desk in court, under oath, if you will protect my grandchildren. — S.K. Rotich"
Halima, to Amani: "He'd decided to stop. Three days too late."

files.text: Stanley Rotich eliminated (deceased); his letter pinned: "The desk was Records." Sagal's "young man from the foundation" and the note signed "M." pinned beside the Ukarimu Foundation.

afterVerdict.beat: In the Pattern File, Rotich's card turns sepia: "eliminated: deceased", in Amani's hand. Notebook: "Records. 'Tell her.' A foundation. A young man called M."
